keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rain, demand and losses determine useful storage
keyPoints.draft: Vukulu bya lwangu, mpfula, xilaveko xa mati na ku lahleka ka mati swi lawula ku hlayisiwa ka mati lama nga tirhisiwaka.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: The size of the roof, rain, water demand and water losses determine storage of usable water.
keyPoints.uncertainty: The four source factors and useful storage are retained; ordinary Xitsonga and the phrase for useful storage need fluent review.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter for the roof
keyPoints.draft: Lulamisa sayizi ya first-flush diverter hi ku landza lwangu naswona yi hlayise.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Set the size of the first-flush diverter according to the roof and maintain it.
keyPoints.uncertainty: The diverter's sizing is linked to the roof and maintenance is required; first-flush diverter remains English as the technical term.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Clear water can still contain germs or chemicals
keyPoints.draft: Clear water ya ha nga va na germs kumbe chemicals.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Clear water can still have germs or chemicals.
keyPoints.uncertainty: Can-still remains explicit; clear, germs and chemicals stay English to avoid implying that clear water is safe.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Testing and treatment must match the intended use
keyPoints.draft: Testing na treatment swi fanele swi fambisana na intended use.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Testing and treatment must correspond with the intended use.
keyPoints.uncertainty: The must-match relation is retained; testing, treatment and intended use remain English anchors.

question.sourceEnglish: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.draft: Hi wahi vuxokoxoko byi lavekaka ku hlawula rainwater tank?
question.literalBacktranslation: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.uncertainty: Rainwater tank remains English as the technical object; question wording is a machine draft.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the province where the farm is located
options.draft: Province ntsena laha farm yi nga kona.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the province where the farm is located.
options.uncertainty: Province and farm remain English; only is retained.

options.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rainfall pattern, water demand and collection losses
options.draft: Vukulu bya lwangu, pattern ya mpfula, xilaveko xa mati na ku lahleka ka mati loko ma hlengeletiwa.
options.literalBacktranslation: The size of the roof, rainfall pattern, water demand and water losses during collection.
options.uncertainty: All four required factors remain present; pattern and roof are mixed-language anchors.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the amount of rain in one storm
options.draft: Ntsengo wa mpfula ya storm yin'we ntsena.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the amount of rain in one storm.
options.uncertainty: Storm remains English; one event and only are explicit.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the price of the biggest available tank
options.draft: Ntsengo ntsena wa tank leyikulu swinene leyi kumekaka.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the price of the biggest tank that is available.
options.uncertainty: Tank remains English; the superlative and only are retained.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand through wet and dry periods. One fixed regional size cannot do that.
rationale.draft: Ku pulana tank swi fanele ku pimanisa supply leyi nga tirhisiwaka na demand hi nkarhi wa wet na dry periods. Sayizi yin'we leyi vekiweke ya region a yi nge endli tano.
rationale.literalBacktranslation: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand during wet and dry periods. One fixed regional size cannot do that.
rationale.uncertainty: The required comparison and rejection of one fixed regional size are retained. Wet and dry periods, supply, demand and region remain English anchors.

question.sourceEnglish: Why does a first-flush diverter matter even for irrigation-only tank water?
question.draft: Ha yini first-flush diverter yi ri ya nkoka hambi mati ya tank ma tirhisiwa eka irrigation ntsena?
question.literalBacktranslation: Why is a first-flush diverter important even when tank water is used for irrigation only?
question.uncertainty: The irrigation-only limitation is retained; first-flush diverter and irrigation remain English technical terms.

options.sourceEnglish: It doesn't matter for irrigation, only drinking water
options.draft: A yi na nkoka eka irrigation; i ya drinking water ntsena.
options.literalBacktranslation: It has no importance for irrigation; it is only for drinking water.
options.uncertainty: The distractor's claim that it matters only for drinking water is retained.

options.sourceEnglish: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops
options.draft: First flush yi rhwala concentrated droppings, dust na pathogens leti nga contaminate edible crops.
options.literalBacktranslation: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops.
options.uncertainty: Concentrated, all three contaminant types, can-contaminate modality and edible crops remain explicit in English.

options.sourceEnglish: It's more acidic and changes soil pH over time
options.draft: It's more acidic naswona yi cinca soil pH hi ku famba ka nkarhi.
options.literalBacktranslation: It is more acidic and changes soil pH over time.
options.uncertainty: The comparative and soil-pH/time claim remain exact English to prevent a shift in distractor meaning.

options.sourceEnglish: It stops the tank overfilling in storms
options.draft: Yi sivela tank ku tala ngopfu hi nkarhi wa storms.
options.literalBacktranslation: It prevents the tank from filling too much during storms.
options.uncertainty: Overfilling and the storm condition remain; storm is kept English.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that later water is safe. Assess quality for the intended use.
rationale.draft: Ku hambukisa early runoff swi nga hunguta contamination, kambe a swi tiyisisi leswaku mati lama taka endzhaku ya hlayisekile. Kambela quality hi ku landza intended use.
rationale.literalBacktranslation: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that later water is safe. Assess quality according to the intended use.
rationale.uncertainty: Can-reduce, no-guarantee, later-water and use-specific assessment are preserved; runoff, contamination and quality remain English anchors.
